paper_title: Learning to Reason under Off-Policy Guidance
caption_used: Training rewards of LLaMA-3.1 8B on the Easy and Hard training sets, displayed as two vertically stacked line plots. In the Easy Training Set (top panel), both Llama-On-Policy-Easy (teal) and Llama-LUFFY-Easy (red) start near 0.0 and increase over 500 steps, with LUFFY reaching approximately 0.4 and On-Policy reaching approximately 0.35 at step 500. In the Hard Training Set (bottom panel), Llama-LUFFY-Hard shows steady improvement from near 0.0 to approximately 0.2 by step 500, while Llama-On-Policy-Hard initially rises to approximately 0.05 before declining back toward 0.0 after step 150. Notably, the performance gap between the two methods is substantially wider on the Easy set, where LUFFY maintains a consistent lead of approximately 0.10 throughout training, compared to the Hard set where their trajectories only clearly diverge after step 200.
model_annotation: The figure presents two vertically stacked line plots comparing the training rewards over steps for two different algorithms, Llama-On-Policy and Llama-LUFFY, on separate training sets: Easy (top) and Hard (bottom). Both plots share the same x-axis, labeled "Steps," which uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 500, with tick labels at intervals of 100. The y-axis, labeled "Training Rewards," is also linear, scaled from 0.0 to 0.4 in the top plot and from 0.0 to 0.2 in the bottom plot. In the top plot, the teal line represents Llama-On-Policy-Easy, starting near 0.0 and rising to approximately 0.35 at step 500. The red line represents Llama-LUFFY-Easy, starting near 0.0 and rising to approximately 0.4 at step 500. In the bottom plot, the teal line represents Llama-On-Policy-Hard, starting near 0.0, rising to approximately 0.05 at step 100, then declining back toward 0.0 after step 150. The red line represents Llama-LUFFY-Hard, starting near 0.0 and steadily increasing to approximately 0.2 by step 500. Both lines in each plot are solid with circular markers and are accompanied by light-colored shaded regions indicating variability or uncertainty around the mean trajectory.
